messages.subject: Enquire .. help!
parts:
Dear Group,

I am now in the process of filtering and re-organizing data that i have collected in the field a few months ago. I counted primates on a survey design created by our group, we decided to, because we found that the area was not accesible in places were DISTANCE suggest that we must set a transect, so we reduce the number of transects to six (previously suggested 10 o more by literature) and choose the systematic random sample, as the most accurate design. So far, i am trying to re-organize the data in stratum, applying the post-stratification strategy. What turns out is, that i did not stratify the data when i was on field, then i am creating stratums according to the positions were i saw the primate, the problem is that i am not sure about the stratum area and i am pretty sure that if i calculate these now, it will be less than the region area.

Please, Could it be possible that stratum area results less than region area?.

My opinion is yes, because we might be representing more than the area of the stratum (which i calculated as the area of the rectangle form by the Lx2w)) as we know that primate from other places of the total area of forest (120 ha) have a home range that cover more than the stratum area.

I hope that information i gave help,

Best regards,
Johana Villota.
